original_value: The local reference frame (LRF) acts as a critical role in 3D local shape description and matching. However, most existing LRFs are hand-crafted and suffer from limited repeatability and robustness. This paper presents the first attempt to learn an LRF via a Siamese network that needs weak supervision only. In particular, we argue that each neighboring point in the local surface gives a unique contribution to LRF construction and measure such contributions via learned weights. Extensive analysis and comparative experiments on three public datasets addressing different application scenarios have demonstrated that LRF-Net is more repeatable and robust than several state-of-the-art LRF methods (LRF-Net is only trained on one dataset). We show that LRFNet achieves 0.686 MeanCos performance on the UWA 3D modeling (UWA3M) dataset, outperforming the closest method by 0.18. In addition, LRF-Net can significantly boost the local shape description and 6-DoF pose estimation performance when matching 3D point clouds.

result.paraphrase: The local reference frame (LRF) plays a crucial role in 3D local shape description and matching. Yet most existing LRFs are manually designed and have limited repeatability and robustness. This paper is the first to learn an LRF with a Siamese network using only weak supervision. Specifically, we contend that every neighboring point on the local surface contributes uniquely to LRF construction, and we quantify these contributions with learned weights. Extensive analysis and comparative experiments on three public datasets covering different application scenarios show that LRF-Net is more repeatable and robust than several state-of-the-art LRF methods, even though LRF-Net is trained on only one dataset. We demonstrate that LRF-Net reaches 0.686 MeanCos on the UWA 3D modeling (UWA3M) dataset, exceeding the nearest method by 0.18. Moreover, LRF-Net can substantially improve local shape description and 6-DoF pose estimation when matching 3D point clouds.
